title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 6-9). M^* is a graded 'cohomology' of formal dimension 2n. L is a degree-2 Lefschetz operator. Σ^* is a graded subalgebra of End^*(M), an abstract stand-in for algebraic correspondences modulo homological equivalence, containing L. The π_i are the Künneth (degree) projectors. Hard Lefschetz (6.1)_i says L^{n-i}: M^i → M^{2n-i} is an isomorphism. This gives the primitive (Lefschetz) decomposition (6.4): for i ≤ n, M^i = ⊕_α L^α P^{i-2α} and M^{2n-i} = ⊕_α L^{n-i+α} P^{i-2α}. The π_{i,α} are the projections onto these pieces.

On this page Grothendieck introduces Λ, of degree -2, by formula (6.5), left blank. From the crossed-out (6.7) it is clearly the unnormalized Lefschetz Λ: Λ(L^α p) = L^{α-1} p for primitive p, and Λ p = 0. This is the Λ of the later 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' and of Kleiman. Check of (6.7):
- On M^i with i ≤ n, LΛ kills exactly the primitive component π_{i,0}. On upper degrees LΛ = 1.
- ΛL fails to be the identity exactly on the components L^{n-i}P^i of M^{2n-i}, which are killed by L. These are the π_{2n-i,0}.
- So LΛ = 1 − Σ_{i≤n} π_{i,0} and ΛL = 1 − Σ_{i≥n} π_{i,0}, with the page-8 indexing convention for the upper half. Both are correct.

Theorem (assuming (6.1)_i for all i). The following are equivalent:
- (i) every inverse (L^{n-i})^{-1} is induced by an element of Σ^{-(2n-2i)}, i.e. (6.2)_i, and π_i ∈ Σ;
- (ii) the algebraic reformulation (6.3)_i: there is w_i ∈ Σ^{-(2n-2i)} with (w_i L^{n-i} − 1)π_i = 0 and (L^{n-i} w_i − 1)π_{2n-i} = 0;
- (iii) Λ ∈ Σ^{-2}.
They further imply:
- (iv) all Lefschetz-decomposition projectors π_{i,α} lie in Σ (his 'isotypic components', i.e. sl2-isotypic);
- (v) the π_i lie in Σ and are the unique family in Σ satisfying the axioms (1.1), (1.3) of the earlier pages.

Proof as written:
- (i) ⇔ (ii) is clear.
- (iii) ⇒ (ii) by taking w_i = Λ^{n-i}. This works because Λ^{n-i} L^{n-i} = 1 on M^i and L^{n-i} Λ^{n-i} = 1 on M^{2n-i}.
- The converse is postponed; page 10 proves (iv) by double induction (ascending in i, descending in α).

In modern terms this is the abstract-algebra form of the equivalent formulations of Standard Conjecture B (Lefschetz type) and of B ⇒ C (algebraicity of the Künneth components). It also gives algebraicity of the primitive-decomposition projectors, inside Grothendieck's unpublished 'Poincaré-Hodge algebra' formalism.

A direct route the page does not take: Λ|_{M^i} = w_{i-2} L^{n-i+1} π_i for i ≤ n, and Λ|_{M^{2n-i}} = L^{n-i-1} w_i π_{2n-i} for i < n. Hence (ii) ⇒ (iii) is immediate. Conversely π_{i,α} = L^α (1 − LΛ) Λ^α π_i, so (iii) ⇒ (iv) is immediate too, without the induction of the next page.
errors: Formula (6.5) defining Λ is left blank on the page; Λ is only implicitly characterized by the crossed-out (6.7).
Degree notation is inconsistent: L ∈ Σ^2 on p.8 but L ∈ Σ^{(1)} (or Σ^{(2)}?) here, and Λ ∈ Σ^{(-2)}. Cohomological degree and Tate-twist indexing seem to be mixed.

At i = n the two definitions of π_{n,α} (lower and upper half) coincide. In (6.7) the index i = n appears in both sums with different meanings (the α=0 piece P^n is counted in both). This is fine but ambiguous, and may be why (vi)/(6.7) was struck out.

The p.8 claim that (6.3) by itself implies π_i ∈ Σ is not justified: (6.3) presupposes the π_i. Unless π_i ∈ Σ is a standing hypothesis, (ii) alone does not obviously give it. Over Q one could use the normalized sl2 relation [L,Λ] = h and interpolate, but that uses (iii).
The proof sketch is incomplete on this page: (i)/(ii) ⇒ (iii) is deferred ('Reste à prouver'), and the uniqueness statement (v) is only gestured at ('au choix ...').

ideas.what: Equivalence of: algebraic inverses of hard Lefschetz isomorphisms (with algebraic Künneth projectors), the existence of w_i satisfying (6.3), and algebraicity of Λ
ideas.modern_name: Equivalent forms of Standard Conjecture B(X) (Lefschetz type) and A(X,L)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles, Bombay 1968/69); Kleiman (Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures, 1968)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles', Algebraic Geometry (Bombay Colloquium 1968), OUP 1969

ideas.what: Unnormalized Lefschetz operator Λ characterized by LΛ = 1 − Σ_{i≤n} π_{i,0}, ΛL = 1 − Σ_{i≥n} π_{i,0}
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz Λ operator (Kleiman/Grothendieck normalization, as opposed to the sl2-normalized one)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hodge/Weil classically; Grothendieck and Kleiman for its algebraic use
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (1969); Kleiman, Dix exposés (1968)

ideas.what: B implies algebraicity of the Künneth projectors and of all primitive-decomposition projectors π_{i,α} ('isotypic components')
ideas.modern_name: B(X) ⇒ C(X); algebraicity of the Lefschetz-decomposition projectors (sl2-isotypic projectors)
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (B ⇒ C); details in Kleiman 1968

ideas.what: Abstract algebraic formalism: graded algebra Σ^* ⊂ End^*(M) with L, Künneth idempotents and axioms (1.1)-(1.4); conjectures restated as purely algebraic conditions
ideas.modern_name: Abstract 'Poincaré/Lefschetz-Hodge algebra' formalism; precursor of Lefschetz modules and Weil cohomology axiomatics
ideas.where_published: Only partially reflected in the 1969 Bombay paper

missed.claim: This is an unpublished draft (1966-67) of the abstract algebraic formalism behind the equivalent forms of conjecture B. It includes the clean characterization of Λ by LΛ = 1 − Σ_{i≤n}π_{i,0}, ΛL = 1 − Σ_{i≥n}π_{i,0}, and the observation that the sl2-isotypic projectors π_{i,α} are in Σ. The mathematics itself is in Kleiman 1968 and Grothendieck 1969; what is undocumented is the abstract 'Poincaré-Hodge algebra' packaging and its date.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck working out B ⇔ Λ algebraic ⇔ algebraic inverses of L^{n-i} in an axiomatic algebra setting before the Bombay paper. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the well-known circle of equivalent forms of Standard Conjecture B and B ⇒ C, plus algebraicity of the Lefschetz-decomposition projectors. All of this was published by Grothendieck (1969) and Kleiman (1968). Only the abstract algebraic framing and the draft character are unpublished.
transcription_corrections: 'Dém. L'équivalence de (i) et (iii) est claire' should read '(i) et (ii)'.
'et le fait que (i) implique par (iii)' should read 'et le fait que (ii) est impliqué par (iii)'.

The theorem header reads 'Les conditions suivantes (i) à (iii) sont équivalentes', with marginal '(6.1)_i et' meaning '(assuming (6.1)_i)'. The marginal insertion is '(ii) Donc les conditions (6.3)_i pour tout i'.
The stray '(ii)' label before 'Ces conditions impliquent de plus' is an overwritten number, probably (iv) or (vi), not a theorem item.
In (vi), 'L ∈ Σ^{(1)}' is uncertain; possibly Σ^{(2)}. 'Σ^{(-2)}' is in the same notation.
Last line: 'On a déjà démontré que ça implique (v)', with '(6.3)' struck out.
Equation label in (vi) is (6.7), overwritten; the whole block (vi) is struck through with large diagonal strokes.
